newsitem.title: USA: Hilton says ITT management unresponsive.
newsitem.headline: Hilton says ITT management unresponsive.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp President Stephen Bollenbach Tuesday, in a pitch to a group of institutional investors for Hilton's $6.5 billion hostile ITT Corp takeover bid, accused ITT's board of directors of being unresponsive to shareholder concerns.
He asked the investors if they could trust ITT's management to take action that would boost shareholder value.
"The first question is can they do the same things that we've said they should do?" Bollenbach asked rhetorically.
"Of course, but it is a question of trust. Why in the world would you trust them to do it? They have never been responsive to the shareholders ever. They won't talk to their shareholders now."

In a speech to a conference sponsored by the Council of Institutional Investors, Ballenbach said ITT, which owns Sheraton Hotels and Caesars World casinos, would be a good fit for the hotel chain. Hilton, he said, wants to make a more aggressive use of its widely recognized name and be a leader in what he said was a consolidating casino gambling business.
"There are tremendous economies of scale in consolidation in the gaming business," Bollenbach said. "There will be a natural consolidation in the gaming business and we want to be a leader in that."
He said the two companies could save about $100 million in operating costs after a takeover.
ITT has rejected Hilton's takeover offer and the two companies are now involved in a lawsuit in Nevada and a proxy fight in an attempt by Hilton to unseat ITT's board of directors.
Hilton wants its bid to go to ITT shareholders for a vote and the company has been asking ITT's largest stockholders to sign an affidavit supporting a legal motion for a mid-May annual meeting.
